newsitem.title: UK: British Gas hit by competition, borrowing.
newsitem.headline: British Gas hit by competition, borrowing.

text.p: British Gas Plc said on Tuesday its first half profits on both a current cost and historical cost basis fell sharply year-on-year as losses on industrial and commercial operations continued to climb due to competition.

Interest payments also rose sharply, to 124 million pounds from 20 million a year earlier, as it borrowed to meet cash demands of its restructuring and planned demerger into two separate companies next year.
On a historic cost basis, first half net profit slipped to 565 million stg from 635 million stg.

On a current cost base first half net profit dropped to 344 million pounds from 429 million. British Gas said the results would have been even worse but for the the cold winter, which boosted operating profits by around 218 million pounds.

The interim dividend was held at 6.4 pence per share, but British Gas warned shareholders that decisions on future dividends can only be made when there is "greater clarity" over the outcome of the battle with regulator Ofgas on prices charged by its gas transmission arm Transco.
"Intense" negotiations with Ofgas are underway, but the two sides are "closer" on a domestic price review, British Gas said.
British Gas said "take or pay" contracts, which oblige it to buy supplies from gas producers at prices well above market rates, continue to "seriously undermine the company's profitability in 1996."
The company said talks with producers on ending the contracts are entering "a more intense phase of negotiation" but warned the process is a slow one.
